clue.text: The case of a killer ?

parts.note: the killer is a gun, and the case is the leather sheath a gunfighter wears at the hip to carry it

explanation.surface: A detective puzzles over the evidence against a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a criminal investigation; it is a container, and the 'killer' is a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's leather sheath, worn on a belt or under the arm, is the container that carries a pistol.

clue.text: See tradesmen about a cape.

indicators.note: about places the word for the tradesmen around the letter a

parts.note: hatters are tradesmen who make or sell hats

explanation.surface: Look at the shopkeepers wearing a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment but is a headland: Cape Hatteras is off North Carolina.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Hatteras is a headland on the North Carolina coast, famous for shipwrecks.

clue.text: Make up card game before 6.50 in the city

indicators.note: make up in a down clue means the pieces are written upward, read in reverse

parts.note: loo is an old card game
pre means before
VI is six and L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Cards to sort out before catching the 6.50 train into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' in a down clue reverses LOO PRE VIL as one run, giving the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is the major port city on the Mersey in north-west England.

clue.text: I sent a fresh decoction

indicators.note: fresh signals the letters are made new, reworked into another order

explanation.surface: I posted a new herbal brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges I SENT A. A tisane is a herbal tea made by steeping or boiling herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal tea is an infusion or brew made by boiling plant material in water.

clue.text: Bird might mate

definitions.meaning: a black crow-like bird that nests in colonies
the castle in chess, a piece able to give checkmate

explanation.surface: A bird that might find a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook is a black crow that breeds in colonies, and the castle piece in chess can deliver checkmate.

clue.text: William went to the county to write

definitions.text: William went to the county to write

parts.words: William went to the county to write
parts.note: the novelist William Somerset ... carried the name of a county in the middle of his own, as if he had gone there to do his writing

explanation.surface: A man called William moves out to the countryside to work on his book.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's full name was William Somerset, then his surname; Somerset is a county in south-west England, so William 'went to the county' in his own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist of Of Human Bondage was christened William Somerset, so the clue describes the author by his first names.

clue.text: Force lots of workers to use temporary expedients

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
a shift is a group of workers on duty together

explanation.surface: Bosses compel staff to cope with stopgap measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshifts are stopgaps, things used for now because nothing better is available.

clue.text: Explosive lava rises following up such an eruption

indicators.note: following says what comes next is placed after the little word up

parts.note: HE is high explosive

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Explosive lava spews upward in a volcanic eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' looks like an adjective for the lava but gives HE (high explosive); 'rises' turns the lava upward in this down clue, and 'following' sets both after 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent upheaval is a great disturbance, like an eruption of the earth.

clue.text: Swell advice to athletes in need of pullovers

definitions.meaning: the rise and fall of the sea, a swell

definitions.text: advice to athletes in need of pullovers
definitions.meaning: the shouted instruction to a tug-of-war team, who are pullers, to haul

explanation.surface: Great tips for sportsmen who need jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: The rising of the sea is its swell, and the cry to a rope-pulling team is the order to pull hard.

clue.text: Diffident ways ?

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Shy manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways' gives two different kinds of way: MODE (a manner) and ST (a street).
explanation.definitionFit: A modest person is unassuming and shy about their own merits.

clue.text: Returning at six to store in Devon

indicators.note: returning means the little word at is read backwards here

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a store or supply of goods is stock

explanation.surface: Coming home at six o'clock to stock up the shop in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns AT into TA. TAVISTOCK is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tavistock is a market town on the western edge of Dartmoor, in that south-western county.

clue.text: Was informed of sound cattle, perhaps

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for cattle is to be said aloud, giving another spelling that matches it

parts.note: cattle are one example of a herd, a group of beasts

explanation.surface: Someone learned the news about some cattle by listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy cattle; it is the signal that a herd is spoken, and the word it sounds like means 'was informed of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have learned of something by being told it is to have caught the news by ear.

clue.text: Mission about to return to mining area

indicators.note: to return says the short word for about is turned backwards

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning, as in business letters
the Rand is the gold-mining region around Johannesburg

explanation.surface: An expedition sets off back to the gold fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns RE into ER. The Rand (Witwatersrand) is South Africa's gold-mining district.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short journey taken to carry out a task, a small mission for someone.

clue.text: Like the detective writer, they apply the acid test.

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective stories

explanation.surface: Testers of metal are compared to a crime novelist who also puts things to the test.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy L. Sayers was a famous English writer of detective fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Assayers test metal ore for purity, and the acid test literally checks whether gold is genuine.

clue.text: Vehicle on river Nile trip-jump on it !

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle
the Po is a river of northern Italy

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of the river's name tumble into new order

explanation.surface: A tour of the Nile, travelling by tram along the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges NILE into LINE. 'Trip' looks like a journey on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung canvas frame that people jump up and down on.

clue.text: A girl without love, who shall be nameless

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the girl's name wraps round the letter for love

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl with no sweetheart is left unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside', so ANN goes round O. Anon is short for anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, marks a writer whose identity is withheld.

clue.text: Regulation observed about one's guns

indicators.note: about says the word for guns is placed around the letter for one

parts.note: ordnance is artillery, big guns
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Gun rules must be kept by every soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ORDNANCE (artillery) round I. The two words are often confused, which the clue uses.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is a decree or by-law, a rule that people are required to keep.

clue.text: Girl is against taking a driver's position-of course!

indicators.note: taking says the first piece takes on the next one, joined to it

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a golfer's stance is how they stand to hit the ball with a driver

explanation.surface: A woman objects to how a motorist sits behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist; 'of course' shows it is a golf club, used on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a girl's name.

clue.text: Cetewayo's pointed arguments ?

parts.note: Cetewayo was the Zulu king who fought the British, and his warriors' sharp points were their spears

explanation.surface: A king's barbed remarks in debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cetewayo (Cetshwayo) was the Zulu king in the 1879 war with Britain; 'pointed arguments' are spears, not barbed words.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the slender iron-tipped throwing spears carried by Zulu warriors.

clue.text: Measure parts of the Isle, of Dogs

parts.note: a span is a measure, the width of a spread hand

indicators.note: parts of means the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Surveying districts of the Isle of Dogs in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' rearranges ISLE into IELS. The Isle of Dogs is a district of east London, which hides 'Dogs' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniels are a group of gun dog breeds with long ears.

clue.text: Contemporary form-filler?

parts.note: a form is a school class, and one who fills it alongside you is your fellow pupil of the same year

explanation.surface: Someone of our time completing official paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like paperwork to fill in; in British schools a form is a class of pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil in the same school year is someone of your own age, sharing the class.

clue.text: Something certain to get cut?

definitions.meaning: racing slang for a certainty or sure thing, also a bargain

explanation.surface: A sure thing that is bound to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sure bet is called a snip in British slang, and a small cut with scissors is also one.

clue.text: Pickwickian makes hesitant start

parts.note: well is a word used to start a sentence
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Dickens character gets off to a stammering start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, er' is how a hesitant speaker starts. Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's cockney manservant in The Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: Carrier joins local squabble

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub, and a bar is a pub
a row is a squabble

explanation.surface: A man joins in an argument at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is British for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a small cart for carrying loads.

clue.text: Rent collector disturbed poet in warehouse

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord's agent bothers a poet living in a storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges RENT and POET together. An entrepot is a port or depot where goods are collected and stored for re-export, which 'collector' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a trading depot or storehouse where goods are held before shipping on.

clue.text: Take steps to find a ship ?

definitions.meaning: to walk heavily or trek a long way
a cargo vessel with no fixed route

explanation.surface: Act to track down a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge along on foot is to tramp, and a cargo ship taking any work it can find is a tramp steamer.

clue.text: Dickensian, used to box ?.

definitions.meaning: Sydney ... is the hero of Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities
a cardboard container used for packing goods

explanation.surface: A Dickens character took up boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney Carton is the self-sacrificing hero of A Tale of Two Cities, and a cardboard pack is a container.

clue.text: Ruler turns up right away

annotationWithheld.why: Ruler turns up right away (4), answer TSAR: no reading of 'turns up right away' gives TSAR (RAST reversed would need a word for it; removing R from any reversal of TSAR plus R gives no word), and no blog or reprint found

clue.text: Climber uses a spike when returning

indicators.note: when returning says the two pieces together are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: a nail is a metal spike

explanation.surface: A mountaineer uses a spike on the way back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when returning' turns A NAIL into LIANA. A liana is a woody climbing plant of tropical forests.
explanation.definitionFit: Lianas are woody vines that climb up rainforest trees toward the light.

clue.text: Cure Nina's disorder, perhaps for life

indicators.note: disorder means the letters are in a muddle and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a woman's illness, possibly for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like Nina's illness; it rearranges CURE NINAS. Life cover is one kind of policy, so 'perhaps for life' defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover against death is one type of policy, so a policy taken out to protect a family on death is an example.

clue.text: D'Artagnan's reply

parts.note: D'Artagnan is the swordsman of The Three Musketeers, and a fencer's reply is a quick return thrust after parrying

explanation.surface: What the musketeer said in answer.
explanation.walkthrough: D'Artagnan, the Musketeers' hero, is a fencer; the word means both a fencing counter-thrust and a quick retort.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing a counter-thrust after a parry has this name, and it also means a sharp verbal comeback.

clue.text: In' rough sea, W.R.N.S. showing inexperience

indicators.note: rough, as of a stormy sea, signals the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Wrens at sea in a storm show they are new to sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SEA and WRNS. The W.R.N.S. was the Women's Royal Naval Service, whose members were called Wrens.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawness describes a raw recruit: being green and untried.
